findings.summary: crates/server/src/sources.rs:144 (refresh) / github.rs prs(): the GitHub source never returns Err, so a read where every repo's PR list failed still sets last_good=now. Observed with both /pulls lists failing: board_source_age_seconds{source="github"} was 8 and the snapshot's last_good was the current time, while all PR data was 36 min old. The app line then reads 'data is 0 min old'. A GitHub outage or rate limit never shows as stale in the age metric or the app, against the metric's own HELP text ('Seconds since the source's last good read').

crates/server/src/github.rs:15,117 (RECENT=20): each read re-reads the records folder and the latest file for every recently merged pipeline PR, at an immutable merge commit, so 2 requests per merged PR. When most of the last 20 closed PRs are pipeline PRs, one read of one repo costs about 42 or more requests, and two repos go past GitHub's 60 an hour in a single burst. The interval spacing can't prevent that. Today booking has only 2 tied merged PRs, so it wasn't hit.

crates/app/tests/board.rs: gate and PR details are asserted only on sub-ticket rows. Removing the top-level card's details(ui, t) call in crates/app/src/lib.rs leaves every app test passing. The top-level rendering was confirmed only by screenshot (TRU-6/TRU-7 cards in app1.png).

Verification environment: the egress proxy adds a GitHub credential to api.github.com requests (no-token curl gets X-RateLimit-Limit 15000). The server sent no token, but its upstream reads (13 this session) were authenticated, so behaviour under GitHub's real 60-an-hour unauthenticated limit could not be observed live. The 45-an-hour spacing is evidenced by the test and the observed 1120 s/1040 s intervals.
